node.title: What is the proper way to suppress a warning in a test file?
node.author: nysus
node.doctext:
I have a test file with Test::NoWarnings. The module getting tested relies on other module that use XS. One of those modules throws a warning that it's "falling back to PP version". This warning causes my test to fail. I tried the following to fix the issue: use strict; use warnings; use File::Path; use Data::Dumper qw(Dumper); use Test::NoWarnings; use Test::Output; use Test::Most tests => 16, 'die'; BEGIN { $ENV{'DANCER_ENVIRONMENT'} = 'testing'; $SIG{__WARN__} = sub { my $warn = shift; return if $warn =~ /fallback to PP version/; warn $warn; }; }

While this does suppress the warning, it also suppresses all warnings that my test might produce making Test::NoWarnings useless. As a workaround, I just comment out the $SIG{__WARN__} stuff while I'm testing but I'd like to learn how to properly address this issue. I tried moving it outside the BEGIN block but that didn't help. Thanks!
